babolat-pure-aero-98-gen8: Spin and easy power with strong serves, but many report elbow or wrist pain.
babolat-pure-aero-98-gen9: More comfortable and controlled than the last generation, though some find it muted and sluggish.
babolat-pure-drive-gen11: Easy power with a softer feel than before; arm discomfort for some, and balls fly long for others.
head-boom-pro-2024: Power, control and stability in one frame, though a couple find it clunky on a one-handed backhand.
head-gravity-pro-2023: Plush, stable feel with comfortable power; the heavy swingweight hurts some one-handed backhands.
head-gravity-tour-2025: Arm-friendly with a good sweet spot for a 98; power is modest, so it suits those who supply pace.
head-radical-mp-2023: Control racket with precision and feel, though modest power and low launch led a few to switch.
head-radical-mp-2025: Softer, arm-friendlier ride with good feel; a couple note it is less powered than the 2023.
head-speed-mp-2022: Balanced all-rounder that many say plays better than later versions; arm soreness for some.
head-speed-mp-2026: Solid, connected feel that is easy on the arm and an improvement on the 2024; a few find it heavy.
tecnifibre-t-fight-300s: Spin, manoeuvrability and power that suit players from modern frames; some added lead for stability.
tecnifibre-t-fight-305s: Quick, manoeuvrable swing with control and stability; many are bothered by the grip shape.
wilson-blade-100-v9: Forgiving, balanced frame with decent power on first serves, though a few felt it lacked character.
wilson-blade-98-16x19-v10: Spin and stability that several find more solid than the V9; scattered gripes of a small sweet spot.
wilson-blade-98-18x20-v9: Stable heavier swing and strong serving; depth and power take more effort, and two found it tiring.
wilson-blade-pro-100-v10: Stable yet whippy with crisp volleys and a strong serve; a couple said it needs extra weight.
wilson-blade-pro-98-16x19-v9: Heavy, feedback-rich frame for strong players, but the very high swingweight is hard to manoeuvre.
wilson-clash-100-pro-v3: Comfortable, stable and controlled for sore elbows; a couple found it unstable against big hitters.
wilson-clash-100-v3: Arm comfort that eased pain from stiffer frames, though power is modest and some find it mushy.
wilson-pro-staff-97-v14: Control and a solid feel for long-time fans of the line; some find it unforgiving or hard on arms.
wilson-shift-99-pro-v1: Spin and power from the denser pattern, though some rec players find it too much racket.
wilson-shift-99-v1: Spin-friendly with a good mix of control and power; a few found it unstable until they added lead.
wilson-ultra-99-pro-v5: Spin and easy power from an open pattern; it punishes mishits and is demanding to swing.
yonex-ezone-100-8th-gen: Easy power and a big sweet spot with comfort close to the Clash; some find the feel muted.
yonex-ezone-98-7th-gen: Control and easy power that many prefer to the newer generation; a few get arm pain.
yonex-ezone-98-8th-gen: Forgiving and easy on the arm with free power, but several dislike the muted, vague feel.
yonex-percept-100: Control and arm comfort with a bigger sweet spot than the 97; limited power means swinging out.
yonex-percept-100d: Precise, stable and arm-friendly with more forgiveness than the 97; the main gripe is limited power.
yonex-vcore-98-7th-gen: Lots of spin and a whippy swing, though others find it underpowered, muted and hard to control.
yonex-vcore-98-8th-gen: Easy power and plenty of spin, but the high launch sends balls long and elbow trouble is common.
